scores.evidence: Phase 5 "Depends on: the Phase 4 sandbox, the Phase 3 retrieval and model access, and Phase 2 HITL and budgets."
scores.rationale: Each phase lists explicit dependencies and the sandbox is proven before resolution is specified; the order runs substrate upward.

scores.evidence: "a real issue on the sandbox repo gets a real comment in production, and its end-to-end trace plus the token and cost metric show up on the dashboard."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real thin end-to-end slice (webhook→queue→LLM→GitHub comment) deployed to production before any features.

scores.evidence: "Autonomy ceiling | The agent never merges... | Per repo and per issue class only: more than 90% of 50+ PRs merged unedited with zero policy violations."
scores.rationale: A table of irreversible decisions gives defaults and concrete flip conditions, including the AI-specific ones.

scores.evidence: "Diff policy gate (widest: it governs every PR)." and Phase 1 permission model "so it goes first"
scores.rationale: Within phases, widest-impact items such as permissions, schema, policy gate and isolation come first, and the plan says so.

scores.evidence: Cross-cutting table Phase 0 Security: "HMAC webhook verification. App key in a secrets manager. Issue body delimited as untrusted. Label output allow-listed."
scores.rationale: Concrete security measures appear in every phase from Phase 0 through 7.

scores.evidence: "One OpenTelemetry trace covers the full path: webhook, queue, LLM call, GitHub API."
scores.rationale: Observability is built in Phase 0 and each later phase has specific traces, metrics and alerts.

scores.evidence: "GitHub Actions builds a container pinned by digest... Infra as code (Terraform). Migrations versioned. Prompt stored in the repo and hashed."
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is covered from Phase 0 (pinned images, IaC, migrations) and in every later phase (frozen eval set, pinned SHAs, versioned fixtures).

scores.evidence: Phase 0 Resilience: "Idempotency on delivery ID. Fast 202 then async. Kill switch. Queue retries with backoff."
scores.rationale: Failure handling has concrete content in every phase, such as dead-letter queue, circuit breakers, fallback model and crash resume.

scores.evidence: "Phase 2: Guardrails, budgets and HITL (AI defenses, before any new capability)" then retrieval, model access, memory, orchestration, routing, feedback in Phases 3–6
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and HITL come before capabilities, and the layers follow the required order, with exit checks for each. Only a minor wrinkle: the memory/orchestration split happens inside Phase 5.

scores.evidence: "Multi-agent orchestration... Pulled forward if the single-loop success rate stops improving and traces show planning failures"
scores.rationale: The deferred list is explicit and every item has a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: An unusually complete plan: it has a real production walking skeleton, explicit gates and flip conditions, security, observability, reproducibility and resilience threaded through every phase, and the AI layers in the right order. I found no significant weaknesses.
